subject: Hexagon Health — usage-evidence-driven GPU top-up and commitment discussion
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@hexagonhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Hexagon Health — usage snapshot + next-step sizing question

Ravi — thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, you mentioned a sustained uptick in token throughput across your inference fleet in March. Can you share the lightweight usage snapshot (avg seq length, p95 latency targets, sustained rps) so we can baseline a short-term top-up suggestion?

I copied Marissa (renewals) and Ben (capacity planning) so we can turn the metrics into a recommended tranche add or a short-term burst bridge. If you have any internal constraints (procurement timelines, target commit date), include those as well.

Next steps I propose:
- You send the usage CSV (Mar snapshot) — quickest is a single csv export.
- We run a 48-hour simulated utilization pass with your profile and share a recommended sizing + cost delta.
- Decide: short-term burst credit vs 3-month committed tranche.

Thanks,
David
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: requested_template.csv (stub)

From: Ravi Singh <ravi@hexagonhealth.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hexagonhealth.ai
Date: 2027-04-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hexagon Health — usage snapshot + next-step sizing question

David — quick turnaround from our side. Attached is the March export you requested (avg seq, p50/p95 latency, token counts by hour). A few notes:
- Peak windows are around 11:00–13:00 EDT and 02:00–03:00 PDT (international traffic).
- Typical sequence length increased from 64 -> 96 after the Q1 rollout of multi-turn summarization.
- Our SRE team can accept a 150ms p95 target for non-critical paths, 80ms for live interactions.

Procurement note: if we move to a committed tranche, procurement needs 30 days minimum for PO + SLA amendment. Ideally we lock numbers by May 10 to have capacity by June.

Attached: hexagon_usage_snapshot_Mar2027.csv (stub)

—Ravi
Head of Platform
Hexagon Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hexagon Health — size simulation notes

Quick pass on the CSV: thanks for sending. High-level read: March shows a 38% increase in average token volume and 1.9x the 95th percentile burst magnitude vs January. Given current model choice (gpt-3.7-like), my initial suggestion:
- Option A (short-term): add a 40% burst pool for 6 weeks (burst credits). Pros: fast, no long-term commit; Cons: higher per-token unit cost.
- Option B (mid-term commit): convert to a 3-month tranche + 20% headroom (recommended) — lowers unit cost and stabilizes latency. Procurement window aligns with their May 10 target.

Action items for sizing run:
1) Run a 48-hour sim with their actual seq distribution and p95 targets (I can run if you confirm the preferred model variant).
2) Produce a cost delta (burst vs commit) + latency SLO table.

I attached a draft proposal (proposed_sizing_v2.pdf stub) that maps GPU counts to throughput assuming H100-equivalent profiles and mixed quantization.

—Ben
Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@hexagonhealth.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hexagon Health — usage-evidence-driven GPU top-up and commitment discussion

Ravi — thanks for the data and the procurement note. Short checklist so we can move toward a PO: 
- Confirm model variant in production (gpt-3.7-like or gpt-4-lite?) — affects GPU sizing significantly.
- Confirm your preferred economic outcome: lower unit price (commit) vs immediate headroom (burst).
- Preferred start date for added capacity (you mentioned June).

If you prefer, we can propose a hybrid: an immediate 6-week burst to cover the April–May ramp, then a 3-month committed tranche starting June 1 with a step-down option depending on measured utilization after 6 weeks. That reduces tail risk for both sides.

I've put a quick timeline in the HubSpot deal (link below) and will prepare a PO-ready SOW once you confirm model and start date. 

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/7239/deal/DEAL-7239

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive — Renewals, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_template.docx (stub)

From: Ravi Singh <ravi@hexagonhealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hexagonhealth.ai, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hexagon Health — usage-evidence-driven GPU top-up and commitment discussion

Marissa / David — that hybrid plan works for us. Answers below:
- Model variant: rolling gpt-3.7-like base for production; we are piloting gpt-4-lite in a subset but not yet at scale. Use gpt-3.7-like for sizing.
- Economic preference: prefer commit for unit cost savings but need the burst to avoid degradation during the ramp.
- Target start: burst immediately (as soon as Redwood can provision), tranche to begin June 1. Procurement will aim to have PO signed by May 15 to meet that date.

Please proceed with the 48-hour sim using gpt-3.7-like profile and share the proposed GPU tranche counts and expected p95 latency under both burst and committed scenarios. Also include an explicit rollback/fallback plan if observed utilization drops below the commit floor after 6 weeks.

Ravi
Head of Platform, Hexagon Health
Attachment: procurement_timeline.pdf (stub)
